in_hebrew.name: עָקֵל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The name Akel is derived from the Hebrew word עָקֵל (עקל), which means 'thorn'. It can also be interpreted as 'one who is pierced' or 'one who is pricked'. In the Bible, the name Akel is associated with the name of a place, Akeldama (אֲכֶלְדָמָה), which means 'field of blood', and the name of a man, Achar (אַחָר), who is described as a man 'of Belial'.

in_greek.name: Ακελ
in_greek.long_meaning: There is no direct Greek equivalent to the Hebrew name Akel. However, the name may have been transliterated as Ακελ in some Greek manuscripts.

in_latin.name: Acel
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Acel is derived from the Hebrew name Akel, which means 'thorn'. It is a rare name in the Latin world and is not associated with any notable figures in history.
